# command: domain to check availability

Add a `domain <name>` command that checks whether a name is free under a list of TLDs. **Motivation:** "there is no way to check new domain name availability" from the terminal when brainstorming project names (the example is `tact`, the author's Tact project).

```bash
$ domain tact
# loop for (.com, .net, etc)
# dig +noall +answer domain
# nslookup domain >/dev/null
```

The note carries the author's TLD shortlist with yearly prices (in roubles) as a hint of the candidate set: `.com 1350`, `.me 880`, `.org 1595`, `.net 1595`, `.info 895`, … `.online`, `.site`, `.tech`, `.cloud`, `.space`, `.blog`, `.shop`, `.group`, `.pro`, `.club`, `.design`, `.art 355`, `.xyz 295`, and so on. A DNS answer is only a heuristic (a registered domain may have no records); a real check needs RDAP/WHOIS. The closing to-do: "port this feature into the `check` project" — i.e. this belongs in a Go tool, not a shell function.
